Question: must legacy import retain raw header evidence to re-emit byte-identical legacy archives?

requirement_or_question: RAR5 is a Tier 2 decode-only adapter; export is not offered because the reference decoder licence forbids reimplementing the compressor. R1 said never RAR or ACE and noted that deletion (WinRAR dropping ACE) beats opt-in flags.

requirement_or_question: RAR5 adapter hazards: readers must skip unknown records, so interpretation-changing records yield silent wrong output; quick-open records are trusted caches (a specified parser differential); names use UTF-8 with private-use-area escapes for unrepresentable Unix bytes; dictionaries reach 64 GB; encryption is PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 plus unauthenticated AES-256-CBC with a 12-byte password check; determinism and the WinRAR 7.23 date are undocumented.
supersession_note: SPEC cites the RAR5 skip mandate and quick-open trust without quoting the technote; appendix supplies primary citations.
research_needed: Quote RAR5 technote wording; construct fixtures with unknown records, PUA names and oversized dictionaries; define adapter refusal rules.

requirement_or_question: Nix NAR is a Tier 2 adapter: trivial to import and a conformance test for canonical serialisation. NAR stores only node type, executable bit, contents, symlink targets and sorted names (no ids, times, xattrs or ACLs), is bit-reproducible, has no index or random access and no in-format compression or dedup; binary caches compress whole NARs with a .narinfo sidecar.
supersession_note: SPEC §14.4 Tier 2; appendix facts feed the fidelity matrix.

Reparse points, symlinks, FIFOs and devices are refused.

requirement_or_question: Structural detection must not rely on archive libraries that normalise or hide behaviour: locate EOCD by backward scan, walk central records by offset arithmetic, re-parse every local header and compare views field by field. The ZIP adapter is hand-written and keeps central, local and descriptor claims as separate observations; a start-to-finish streaming ZIP read cannot be correct because local headers are unreliable.

requirement_or_question: Strict ZIP refuses: input without an EOCD signature, multi-disk/spanned archives, bytes between central directory end and EOCD (including unconditional ZIP64 end records and CD digital signatures), general-purpose flags outside bits 1-3 and 11 (enhanced deflate, patched data, masked headers, reserved), duplicate ZIP64 extras, sentinels without ZIP64 extras, and ZIP64 extras with bytes beyond sentinel-required values; unknown methods and encryption are refused.

requirement_or_question: Local ZIP64 extras are read with only size sentinels as required values, so writers emitting full or zero-filled local ZIP64 extras without 0xFFFFFFFF sentinels (common in streaming writers) would be refused as contradictory unrequested values.

requirement_or_question: Strict ZIP requires the EOCD comment to end at EOF and refuses trailing bytes, but does not require the first local header at offset 0, contiguous entries or explained gaps, so SFX stubs and inter-entry hidden data are neither refused nor recorded (unlike 7z). Trailing data is rare in registries but common in SFX installers; concatenated ZIPs with two central directories were used for AV evasion in 2024 (7-Zip reads the first, WinRAR both).
research_needed: Fixtures with prepended stubs, gaps, hidden inter-entry data and concatenated archives; per-reader outcomes; decide Omission versus Irreconcilable evidence.
decision_needed: Whether strict ZIP must record or refuse unexplained prefix/gap bytes and how SFX/concatenated archives are reported.

requirement_or_question: Overlapping physical entry extents (local header start to data or descriptor end) are Irreconcilable and refused with ZipOverlappingExtent in every import mode; malformed or truncated framing and arithmetic outside policy are refused and no entry is ever skipped (all-or-nothing import).

R3 EB-Z019 shows Info-ZIP extracts the extra name while libraries report the CD name. A name like a/b splits into components or fails under strict, with the receipt recording which.

Every compat resolution is stored with profile ID, rule, chosen and rejected observations; compat records Divergence resolutions for central/local name or method differences, resolves mtime from the selected name header only, and refuses divergences outside {filename, compression_method, crc32, compressed_size, uncompressed_size} such as flags, DOS time and attributes.

requirement_or_question: Divergence: assertions differ but are representable and policy-resolvable (e.g. two mtimes); refused under --strict, resolved by the named runtime under --compat. Irreconcilable: assertions imply different content or structure (declared size versus actual stream, duplicate names); always refused under --strict. The compatibility predicate separating Refinement from Divergence is undefined; DOS local-time versus UTC extended timestamps may make most real ZIP mtimes Divergence.
